standard: Visible refinement acceptable at application scale; not a numerical quality score or release approval.

front.note: The rug now has a smooth round textile edge and a shallow sun motif instead of a polygonal disc with folded leaf-like rays.

rear.note: The opposite view preserves the round outline and peach center, with the original ray layout retained as restrained surface relief.

detail.note: Full-size inspection shows the ray outlines as shallow inlays in the thicker foundation. The retained white-on-white default is subtle, so the rays read best at close placement scale.

underside.note: The backing is closed and the circular edge is continuous, without the previous long straight polygon segments.

clay.note: Clay confirms the smooth circular foundation and low relief. This improves the rug construction; it does not claim strong color contrast or a photoreal textile.

front.note: The seat now has a continuous tailored edge and rounded corners without projecting black support tips.

rear.note: The original wraparound back and arm supports remain attached, with the corrected seat fitted inside the shell.

detail.note: Full-size inspection confirms a consistent, seated welt and quiet cover surface; the former corner puckers and buried piping are gone.

underside.note: The support pan is contained inside the cushion and the extended original column meets the seat assembly without the former gap.

clay.note: Clay confirms the coherent rounded rectangular cushion and continuous seam while preserving the original barrel-chair silhouette.

front.note: The seat retains its rounded rectangular form with an even seam and no exposed black pan corners.

rear.note: The original separate back remains aligned over the fitted seat and pedestal.

detail.note: The close view shows continuous piping seated on the cover, replacing the former irregular corner folds.

underside.note: The support pan stays within the cushion outline and the swivel column now meets the seat underside.

clay.note: Clay confirms that the smoother seat edge and support contact are geometric corrections, preserving the chair's original proportions.

front.note: Five evenly spaced drawer fronts now match the catalog name within the unchanged tall cabinet envelope.

rear.note: The original closed rear, cable port and toe kick remain unchanged and aligned.

detail.note: The close view confirms five distinct static fronts and five matching recessed pulls with consistent gaps.

underside.note: The closed base and inset plinth remain supported beneath the corrected five-front arrangement.

clay.note: Clay confirms the five-drawer exterior; this correction does not claim newly animated or mechanically operable drawers.

front.note: The table retains its original slab while its two stone arches now meet rectangular piers with matching stock width.

rear.note: The opposite supports have coherent arch-to-pier transitions instead of the previous rounded overhanging sleeves.

detail.note: The close view preserves the smooth slab edge and shows restrained block joints at the fitted pier tops.

underside.note: Full-size inspection confirms clean semicircular openings and supported bridge ends, without the former scalloped dark notches.

clay.note: Clay shows continuous arch silhouettes seated beneath the tabletop. Small visible stone block joints are an acceptable construction detail.

front.note: The linen shade retains its open lined construction above the timber tripod, with the spreader now reaching all three legs.

rear.note: The fitted spreader and original splayed legs remain coherent from the opposite side, within the original lamp envelope.

detail.note: The close view shows the enlarged spreader meeting the timber legs instead of floating between them.

underside.note: Full-size inspection shows the added central hub and thin shade support spokes. Source inspection corrected the earlier cap inference: the bright area is the existing inner shade wall, which remains open.

clay.note: Clay preserves the original shade and tripod silhouette while showing the fitted supports. The added socket and bulb use existing material roles without changing emission factors.
